dimensions.assessment: Affects state, local, tribal, and nonprofit entities eligible to receive grants for water project navigator positions.
dimensions.evidence: eligible entity means (A) a State; (B) an Indian Tribe; (C) any acequia, land grant-merced, local government, water supplier, special district

dimensions.assessment: Provides funding and administrative assistance mechanisms to help resource-limited entities develop complex water infrastructure projects.
dimensions.evidence: assist the eligible entity in planning, developing, and implementing multi-benefit water projects, including grant writing, project management, technical assistance

dimensions.assessment: Sets a maximum expenditure limit of $15,000,000 of Federal funds in any single fiscal year, with a standard 75 percent federal cost-share cap.
dimensions.evidence: Not more than $15,000,000 of Federal funds may be expended in any 1 fiscal year to carry out this Act.

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a new federal grant program, sets specific project criteria, prioritizes disadvantaged communities, and requires congressional reporting.
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary shall establish a program to support the development and implementation of multi-benefit water projects... to be known as the 'Water Project Navigators Program'

dimensions.assessment: Limits individual grants or agreements to a maximum initial period of 3 years, with potential extensions of up to 2 additional years.
dimensions.evidence: a grant or cooperative agreement under the Program shall be limited to a period of not more than 3 years.

importance_detail.rationale: The bill establishes the Water Project Navigators Program within the Department of the Interior to award grants and cooperative agreements supporting multi-benefit water projects.
